title: Global intertwiner I(φ_y, φ_x) = K_x G^(0) K_y
body_html:
Global intertwiner identity $I(\phi_y, \phi_x) = K_x G^{(0)} K_y$

Proposition. For $x, y \in A^{(0)}$, $$I(\phi_y, \phi_x) = K_x\, G^{(0)}\, K_y.$$
proof_html:
Induct on the length $d$ of the twisted Levi sequence $G^{(0)} \subseteq G^{(1)} \subseteq \cdots \subseteq G^{(d)} = G$.

Base case $d = 0$. Trivial: $G = G^{(0)}$, so the LHS $I(\phi_y, \phi_x)$ is just the intertwiner of the level-zero character on $G^{(0)}$, and the RHS $K_x G^{(0)} K_y = G^{(0)}$ exhausts the same.

Inductive step. Apply the two-term intertwiner identity (Two-term intertwiner I(φ_y, φ_x) = G_{x,s} G' G_{y,s} (Yu Thm 9.4 generalized)) to the outer pair $(G^{(d-1)}, G^{(d)})$ with the depth-$r_{d-1}$ character $\phi_{d-1}$: $$I_{G^{(d)}}(\hat\phi_{d-1, y}|_{J_y},\, \hat\phi_{d-1, x}|_{J_x}) \;=\; G^{(d)}_{x, s_{d-1}}\, G^{(d-1)}\, G^{(d)}_{y, s_{d-1}}.$$

Intersecting with the relations from lower strata (encoded in $\phi = \prod_{i=0}^d \hat\phi_i$) and using the intersection factorization $${}^g K_{y,+} \cap K_{x,+} \;=\; ({}^g K^{(d-1)}_{y, +} \cap K^{(d-1)}_{x, +}) \cdot ({}^g J_y \cap J_x), \tag{$\dagger$}$$ the recursive identity $$I(\phi_y, \phi_x) \cap G^{(d-1)} \;=\; I_{G^{(d-1)}}(\phi_y|_{K^{(d-1)}_{y, +}},\, \phi_x|_{K^{(d-1)}_{x, +}})$$ holds. By inductive hypothesis the RHS is $K^{(d-1)}_x G^{(0)} K^{(d-1)}_y$. Combining with the two-term identity at the top stratum yields $I(\phi_y, \phi_x) = K_x G^{(0)} K_y$. $\square$

The factorization ($\dagger$) is Yu Lemma 13.7 in the original notation. After Fintzen 2021, the proof of ($\dagger$) is reformulated in [Dat–Fintzen 2026 §3.4] as a lattice-intersection identity, applicable in any tame twisted Levi tower under the (now-explicit) $p$-hypothesis; see Fintzen 2021: correction to Yu's tame supercuspidal construction and the parallel table in [[node:references.yu_construction|yu_construction § Dat-Fintzen parallel]].

Support corollary

Lemma. For $x \in A^{(0)}$, $z \in \BSigma$, $$\Hom_{K_{z,+} \cap K_{x,+}}(\phi_z, \phi_x) \ne 0 > \;\Longrightarrow\; z \in K_x \mathcal{B}^0.$$

In particular, $\varphi \in C_\bullet(\BSigma, V)[\phi_x]$ has support contained in $K_x \cdot \mathcal{B}^0$.

This proves the support lemma [[node:coefficient_systems.support_in_BSx]] in the tame case.
